lines: Tellement que s'il a ſongé ceſte nou-
uelle impudẽce, & impoſture, ne s'en faut
Bien que la loy preſume des hommes, que chacun eſt
bon, bien viuant, & d'honneſte conuerſation {a}, & que
nul d'eux ha intention de mal faire {b}: toutesfois en ce-
luy qui vne fois a eſté mauuais & ſurprins en quelque
meſchanceté, la loy à grande raiſon penſe & le preſume
eſtre touſiours tel, en la meſme eſpece de mauuaiſtié {c}.
comme par exemple vn qui aura quelquefois deſrobé,
ſ'il eſt derechef accuſé de larrecin, pour ſi petite preuue
d'autre coniecture qu'il y aye, facilement ou le preſu-
mera pour le iourd'huy eſtre laron. Et elle qui aura vne
fois paillardé, qu'elle mal-verſe encores: & cil qu'il
en la premiere accuſatiõ aura eſté calomniateur, l'eſtré
encor en la ſeconde {d}. Deſquels & ſemblables, la raiſõ
n'eſt pas mal-aiſée à entendre: car il eſt vray-ſemblable
qu'en la volonté de fait, ou de parole declarée, chacun
d'accident, ou qualité (qui conſiſte en fait) facilement
ne ſe preſume point {f}. Ains pluſtoſt on tire argument
& coniecture du paſſé, au temps preſent & a l'aduenir {g}:
comme celuy qu'on a cognu vne fois riche, on le pre-
ſume encor pour le iourd'huy riche, ou pauure; encor
pauure. vn qui a eſté ſeigueur d'vn lieu, l'eſtré par apres:
vn ſuiet, l'eſtre encores. & ainſi des ſemblables {h}.
Au contraire, que le priſonnier fuſt veri-
tablement Martin Guerre, y auoit trente
eſtoyent les quatre ſeurs dudit Martin,

uncertain.note: Page overview. Clean CUDL colour scan, even inking, no tears; a brown damp/foxing stain across the top-left corner and upper margin does not touch the type. Furniture: folio '58' top left (matches the manifest), running head 'ARREST DV' in spaced capitals closed up, headings 'TEXTE.', 'ANNOTAT. XXXVII.' and (the second) 'TEXTE' in spaced capitals, no signature, no catchword, no ornament or decorated initial, no foot citation block (foot.jpg is blank below the last body line; body-8.jpg is blank paper). A strip of the facing recto at the gutter (right) edge is ignored. Layout: one carry-over line of the previous annotation, then TEXTE (3 lines of large type), then ANNOTAT. XXXVII (23 lines), then TEXTE (5 lines of large type, running on to the next page). The page ends about a third of the way down with white space below the last line. Marker alphabet: the carry-over line closes the previous annotation with {k}; the new annotation restarts at a and runs a-h with no gaps.

NO KEY LETTER IS PRINTED on this two-line note ('Panor' au c. ij.' / 'de maled.'), so it is recorded with key null per §4. Its first line stands level with the second line of the large-type TEXTE, i.e. two lines below the body's only marker {k} ('volonté {k}.', blocks[0].lines[0]); it is almost certainly the citation for marker {k}, carried over from the previous annotation, but nothing keys it. Marker {k} therefore has no keyed margin_notes/foot_notes entry. The opening 'P' sits at the same left edge as the key letters a-h and is the P of 'Panor'' (Panormitanus), not a key. The mark after 'Panor' is a raised comma-shaped abbreviation stroke, transcribed as an apostrophe; 'Panor'au' is set tight and normalized to two words.

uncertain.text: uelle impudẽce, & impoſture, ne s'en faut
uncertain.note: 'impudẽce': the mark over the e is a flat, slightly wavy horizontal bar, quite unlike the steep thick diagonal of the acute in 'ſongé' (line 0) and 'impoſture' has none; read as the nasal tilde (= impudence), not an acute. A reader working from the shape alone could write 'impudéce'. Also: 's'il' (line 0) and 's'en' (line 1) both have a ROUND s in this large type, and 'esbahir' (line 2) a round s before b, against the long ſ of 'ſ'il' in the small annotation type (blocks[4].lines[7]).

uncertain.text: fois paillardé, qu'elle mal-verſe encores: & cil qu'il
uncertain.note: 'cil' is set with a visible justification gap between the c and the il ('& c il qu'il'); transcribed as the single word 'cil' (= celui) per the §1 word-division rule. The mark after 'encores' is a colon (two round dots), and 'mal-verſe' carries a true mid-line hyphen.

uncertain.text: en la premiere accuſatiõ aura eſté calomniateur, l'eſtré
uncertain.note: sic: 'l'eſtré' carries a clear acute on the final e (same steep stroke as 'eſté' earlier in the line), although the word is l'estre; the same spelling recurs at blocks[4].lines[21] ('l'eſtré par apres:'), while blocks[4].lines[22] has plain 'l'eſtre'. Transcribed as printed in all three places.

uncertain.text: comme celuy qu'on a cognu vne fois riche, on le pre-
uncertain.note: the line-end word-break sign after 'pre' is a small round dot raised to mid x-height, not the horizontal bar used at 'ce-' (lines[2]) or 'veri-' (blocks[6].lines[0]); the same raised mid-dot ends 'preſu-' (lines[8]). Both transcribed as '-' per §1 (the p046 ruling on the raised mid-dot).

uncertain.text: ſume encor pour le iourd'huy riche, ou pauure; encor
uncertain.note: the mark after 'pauure' is read as a SEMICOLON: the upper element is a small round dot and the lower one is a narrow vertical blob with a short tail at the baseline, unlike the two evenly round dots of the page's certain colons ('entendre: car', 'faire {b}:', 'encores:'), and unlike the long curving tail of the comma after 'riche' on the same line. A colon is the plausible alternative.

uncertain.text: pauure. vn qui a eſté ſeigueur d'vn lieu, l'eſtré par apres:
uncertain.note: WRONG SORT, sic: 'ſeigueur' for seigneur. At 7x the letter after the g is unmistakably a u (two stems joined by a round bottom bow), not an n; compare the n of 'vn' on the same line. Transcribed as printed. A faint stray ink arc (a thin curved line, probably offset or a pen slip) crosses this line and the one above between 'lieu' and 'apres'; it is not type and is not transcribed.

the mark after 'teſmoins' is a round baseline period (set with a space on each side), not a comma, although a lower-case 'entre' follows; transcribed as printed and the spacing normalized. The page uses mid-sentence periods freely ('laron. Et elle', 'pauure. vn qui', 'encores. & ainſi').

the line opens with an italic CAPITAL P followed by a space and 'rogo.'; at 12x the sort has an ordinary foot serif and NO stroke through stem or descender, so it is not ꝑ/ꝓ. The citation wants the paragraph sign ('§ rogo', Dig. de legatis ij, l. cum pater), so this is probably a wrong sort or a printer's substitute for §; transcribed as the letter printed.

the p of 'p̃te' carries an abbreviation stroke: a short horizontal bar crossing the top of the stem and projecting to its left, absent from every other p on the page ('paruu', 'ſump.', 'pro', 'proba', 'præterea'). Transcribed as p + combining tilde per §2; 'ꝑte' is the alternative rendering if the reconciler reads the bar as crossing the descender. The intended citation is presumably 'de p[rae]ſump[tionibus]', the line running on to 'ſump.'. 'ſcribã' has a straight bar (tilde) over the a.

sic: the line ends 'poſti' and runs on to 'dens' — i.e. the print gives 'poſtidens' where the citation wants 'poſſidens'. At 16x the second tall letter has a clear crossbar and a curled top (the italic t), not the plain descending stroke of a long ſ; compare the unambiguous 'poſ-' / 'ſideris' break in note h. Probably a wrong sort (t for ſ); transcribed as printed.

the mark closing the line is read as a comma (short tail below the baseline) rather than a period; 'nõ' has a straight bar over the o. In the next line a period genuinely follows the ampersand (a solid baseline dot, the same size as the period after 'cond'), and the print sets it tight, '&.'; the §1 spacing rules ('& takes a space on both sides', 'no space before a period') collide there, and the validator's normalizer resolves it as '& .', which is what the line carries. The reconciler may prefer '&.'.

beside_line values were fixed by measuring row centres in pages/read/p058.jpg: the margin is set solid in a smaller face with tighter leading than the body, so entries drift relative to their markers (note g, for instance, begins six body lines above its {g}). Each beside_line is the body line whose centre is nearest the note's first line, accurate to about half a line; note b's first line falls almost exactly between 'nul d'eux…' (which carries {b}) and 'luy qui vne fois…' (given here).

Spacing normalized throughout per §1: words set tight ('quesil', 'nesen', 'toutesfoisen', 'lelaron', 'yauoit', 'Panor'au', 'proſoc.', 'l.merito.D.', 'lus,au', 'reg.iur.', 'ſcribã.de', 'ſump.c.paruu', 'li.xxij.q.v.', 'D.de cond.&.', 'ſol.l.ſiue', 'ba.c.præterea', 'ſideris.allegu.'), spaces set before punctuation by justification ('esbahir .', 'paillardé ,', 'teſmoins .', 'ſemblables ,', 'dens .C.') and the space inside the closing parenthesis of '(qui conſiſte en fait )facilement'. Nothing added or removed beyond spacing. Long-s findings double-checked at 5x or more: 'paſſé', 'l'aſſeuroient' are ſſ; no ſs spelling occurs on the page; 'toutesfois', 'esbahir', 's'il', 's'en', 'des', 'les' keep the round s as printed.
